items.label: PR states the problem and links the issue
items.why: Reviewers judge code against intent; without it they end up reviewing style.

items.label: Code achieves the stated intent and acceptance criteria
items.why: A clean diff that solves the wrong problem is still wrong.

items.label: One logical change, no unrelated edits
items.why: Mixed concerns hide bugs and make the change hard to revert.

items.label: Size is reviewable, or split into clear steps
items.why: Defect detection drops sharply past a few hundred changed lines.

items.label: Change lives in the module that owns the responsibility
items.why: Logic in the wrong layer gets duplicated and drifts.

items.label: No new dependency cycles or layer violations
items.why: Dependency direction is expensive to undo once callers rely on it.

items.label: Reuses existing patterns instead of adding a second convention
items.why: Two ways to do one thing doubles the maintenance and the bugs.

items.label: API, schema and contract changes are intentional and called out
items.why: Silent contract changes break callers outside the diff.

items.label: Builds, typechecks and lints clean (verified, not assumed)
items.why: A diff can read correctly and still not compile against the rest of the code.

items.label: Logic is correct, including null, empty, boundary and concurrent cases
items.why: Edge cases are where reviewers add the most value over tests.

items.label: Errors are handled at the right level; nothing is swallowed
items.why: Swallowed errors turn failures into wrong answers.

items.label: Names and structure make intent obvious; no dead code
items.why: The next reader pays for every unclear name.

items.label: Tests exercise the changed behavior
items.why: Line coverage without behavior assertions proves nothing.

items.label: Edge and failure cases are covered
items.why: Happy-path tests miss the bugs that reach production.

items.label: A bug fix includes a test that fails without the fix
items.why: Without it the bug can return unnoticed.

items.label: Tests are deterministic and isolated
items.why: Flaky tests get ignored, then deleted.

items.label: No new allocations, queries or IO in hot loops; complexity justified
items.why: Performance regressions rarely show up in a review-sized test.

items.label: Resources are disposed; no unbounded growth
items.why: Leaks surface in long runs, far from the change that caused them.

items.label: Untrusted input is validated; no SQL, path or command injection
items.why: Injection bugs are cheap to prevent and expensive to find later.

items.label: No secrets or PII in code, config or logs
items.why: Leaked secrets need rotation; leaked PII needs disclosure.

items.label: Comments explain why where the code is not obvious
items.why: The diff context disappears after merge; the comment stays.

items.label: Docs and changelog updated for user-visible or contract changes
items.why: Stale docs mislead more than missing docs.

items.label: Follows repo conventions (AGENTS.md, coding standards)
items.why: Consistency keeps the codebase searchable and predictable.

items.label: Branch and commit messages follow the repo's rules
items.why: History is the first place anyone looks when this breaks.

items.label: Deploy, migration and rollback path is clear
items.why: A change you cannot back out turns a bug into an outage.

items.label: Failures are diagnosable from logs or metrics
items.why: You debug production with what you logged, not what you meant to log.

items.label: Follow-ups are tracked, not left as TODOs
items.why: Untracked TODOs become permanent.
